findings.title: Controller requires params[:group_id] but routes are member routes requiring :id
findings.body: The `add_members` action (line 66) and `remove_member` action (line 85) both call `params.require(:group_id).to_i`. However, the routes `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` are written directly inside `resources :groups do ... end` in `config/routes.rb`, not inside a `collection do ... end` block. In Rails, direct routes at this nesting level are treated as member routes, producing URLs like `DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members` (where `:id` is the group ID). The JS client sends `DELETE /admin/groups/{id}/members.json` which matches the member-route pattern, but then `params[:group_id]` is never populated, so every call raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing: param is missing or the value is empty: group_id`. The admin group-member add/remove feature is therefore entirely broken. To fix, either move the routes into a `collection do ... end` block and have the client pass `group_id` as a query/body parameter, or change the controller to read `params[:id]`.

findings.title: Test invokes remove_member with xhr :put but route is DELETE
findings.body: At line 115, `it "cannot remove members from automatic groups"` does `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`. The route for `remove_member` is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (HTTP method DELETE). No PUT route exists for this action, so Rails cannot match the request and the test will fail with `ActionController::UrlGenerationError`. The HTTP verb in the spec must match the route verb.

findings.title: Tests pass group_id but the member routes require :id in the URL
findings.body: The `add_members` test (line 103) and `remove_member` tests (lines 115, 125) pass `group_id: group.id` as a request parameter. Because the routes are member routes that require `:id` in the URL path, Rails' URL generator cannot find `:id` in the parameters and will either raise `ActionController::UrlGenerationError` or substitute `group_id` for `:id` and produce an unintended URL. The tests must pass `id: group.id` (with the controller updated to read `params[:id]`), or the routes must be rewritten as collection routes.

findings.title: Redundant group.save after users.delete and swallowed errors
findings.body: In `remove_member`, `group.users.delete(user_id)` calls `ActiveRecord::Associations::CollectionAssociation#delete`, which directly issues a SQL DELETE on the join record and is already persisted. The subsequent `group.save` therefore has no unsaved changes to commit and cannot fail because of the deletion. The `if group.save / else render_json_error(group)` branching is misleading. Additionally, any DB-level error raised by `delete` (FK violations, lock timeouts, etc.) is not rescued, so the controller would 500 instead of returning a clean JSON error.

findings.title: Silent failure on non-existent usernames in add_members
findings.body: In `add_members`, when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns nil, the `if user = ...` branch silently skips that entry. The action still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if zero users were actually added. Admins therefore have no signal that a typo or non-existent account caused some (or all) intended members to be dropped. The action should accumulate the missing usernames and return them in the response, or return a non-success status when any username is unknown. The same applies to usernames that contain stray whitespace after splitting on commas (`"a, b"` produces `" b"`).

findings.title: Stray closing with no matching opening tag
findings.body:
Line 19 contains a `` inside the `{{#each m in members}}` block but there is no corresponding opening `
` anywhere in the template. This is invalid HTML and will produce browser parser warnings and an unexpected DOM tree (the browser will silently ignore the orphaned closer, or restructure siblings). Either remove the stray tag or wrap the rows in a matching element.

findings.title: findMembers returns undefined instead of a resolved promise when name is empty
findings.body: When `this.get('name')` is empty, the function executes `return ;` which yields `undefined`. The previous version returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. This violates the implicit promise-returning contract of a `find*` method: any caller that chains `.then(...)` will throw `TypeError: Cannot read property 'then' of undefined`. While the immediate callers in this PR (`admin_group_route.js`, `group-members.js.es6`, `admin-group.js.es6`) happen not to chain, future callers will. The function should return `Ember.RSVP.resolve()` (or at minimum `[]` so callers awaiting `.length` don't break) when name is blank.

findings.title: Race condition: members load after the template has already rendered
findings.body: `setupController` calls `model.findMembers()` but does not return its promise, so Ember does not wait for the AJAX request to finish before the template renders. The `{{#each m in members}}` block in `group/members.hbs` will therefore render with `members` undefined for a brief flash of empty content, then re-render when the promise resolves. The previous implementation used `afterModel` whose returned promise was awaited by the router before `setupController` ran, guaranteeing the data was ready. This is a UX regression and should be fixed either by returning the promise from `setupController` or by reverting to `afterModel` (or by toggling a loading flag in the controller until `findMembers` resolves).
